blockers.finding: The prospective DU parent starts its 120000ms clock after filesystem, disk, STOP, preparation-intent and ledger reads, so preflight is uncharged and a depleted parent can still spawn with a 1ms timeout.

The runner statically imports canonical capability and process code before its own source/runtime/production validation. DU verifies only runner and manifest bytes, so canonical code can execute before refusal. The parent must validate the frozen source, production files, runtime modules and preparation-intent hash before importing trusted canonical code or spawning.
DU reads mutable preparation-intent.json without checking its byte hash, then copies its runtime bindings into authority.

DU uses spawnSync and unguarded exclusive writes. Publication failure can omit a durable terminal after a charged child. Preexisting paths, all settlement writes and a fallback refusal need explicit handling. Owned process settlement must be recorded through runOwnedProcess; its claim remains limited to its process group and observed descendants.

A zero exit is only a child result requiring review. Root must independently reconcile canonical terminal/result/metadata-attempt identities, exact charge/usage, reservation release, STOP state and output hashes.
